का.आ. 598.--भारत सरकार ने पेट्रोलियम और खनिज पाइपलाइन (भूमि मे उपयोग के अधिकार का अर्जन) 
अधिनियम, 4962 (4962 का 50) जिसे इसमे इसके पश्चात उक्त अधिनियम कहा गया है) की धारा 3 कि उपधारा (॥) के 
अधीन जारी भारत सरकार के पेट्रोलियम और प्राकृतिक गैस मंत्रालय की अधिसूचना संख्या का. आ. 2969(अ) तारीख 


24.07.2024 जो भारत के असाधारण राजपत्र तारीख 25.07.2024 मे प्रकाशित की गई थी, द्वारा उस अधिसूचना से 
संलग्न अनुसूची में विनिर्दिष्ट भूमि में मैसर्स इंद्रधनुष गैस ग्रिड लिमिटेड द्वारा असम राज्य में सिलचर सीजीडी ae लाइन 
ऑफ गुवाहाटी-शिलांग-सिलचर-पानीसागर प्रकृतिक गैस पाइपलाइन के मधायम से प्रकृतिक गैस के परिवहन के लिए 
पाइपलाइन बिछाने के प्रयोजन के लिए उपयोग के अधिकार का अर्जन करने के अपने आशय की घोषणा की थी; 


और उक्त राजपत्रित अधिसूचना की प्रतियाँ जनता को उपलब्ध करा दी गई थी; 
और सक्षम प्राधिकारी ने जनता से प्राप्त आक्षेपों को परीक्षण के उपरांत निपटान कर दिया है; 


और सक्षम प्राधिकारी ने, उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 6 की उप - धारा () के अधीन भारत सरकार को अपनी 
रिपोर्ट दे दी है; 


[भागवा--खण्ड 3(3)]_  भारतका राजपत्र : अप्रैल 8, 2026/चैत्र 28, 948 30085 
और भारत सरकार ने, उक्त रिपोर्ट पर विचार करने के पश्चात और यह संतुष्ट हो जाने पर कि उक्त भूमि 
पाइपलाइन बिछाने के लिए अपेक्षित है, उसमें उपयोग के अधिकार का अर्जन करने का विनिश्चय किया है; 


अतः अब, भारत सरकार, उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 6 कि उपधारा (॥) द्वारा प्रदत शक्तियों का प्रयोग करते हुये, 
यह घोषणा करती है कि इस अधिसूचना से संलग्न अनुसूची में विनिर्दिष्ट भूमि में पाइपलाइन बिछाने के लिए उपयोग के 
अधिकार का अर्जन किया जाता है; 


और भारत सरकार, उक्त अधिनियम कि धारा 6 कि उपधारा (4) द्वारा प्रदत शक्तियों का प्रयोग करते हुये, यह 
निर्देश देती है कि पाइपलाइने बिछाने के लिए भूमि मे उपयोग के अधिकार, इस घोषणा के प्रकाशन की तारीख को, भारत 
सरकार में निहित होने के बजाय, पाइपलाइन बिछाने का प्रस्ताव करने वाली मैसर्स इंद्रधनुष गैस ग्रिड लिमिटेड में निहित 
होगा और तदुपरि, भूमि में ऐसे उपयोग का अधिकार, इस प्रकार अधिरोपित निबंधनों और शर्तों के अधीन रहते हुये, सभी 
विलंगमों से मुक्त, मैसर्स इंद्रधनुष गैस ग्रिड लिमिटेड में निहित होगा।

MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
New Delhi, the l0th March, 2026 


5.0. 598.—Whereas by notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural 
Gas S.O.No.2969(E) dated the 24.07.2024, issued under sub-section (l) of section 3 of the Petroleum and Minerals 
Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 962 (50 of 962), (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), 
published in the Extra Ordinary Gazette of India dated the 25.07.2024, the Government of India declared its intention 
to acquire the Right of User in the land specified in the Schedule appended to that notification for the purpose of 
laying pipeline for transportation of Natural Gas through Silchar CGD Spur line of Guwahati - Shillong - Silchar - 
Panisagar Section of North - East Natural Gas Pipeline in the state of Assam by Indradhanush Gas Grid Limited 
(IGGL). 


And whereas copies of the said Extraordinary Gazette notification were made available to the public. 


And whereas the objections received from the public to the laying of the pipeline have been considered and 
disposed by the Competent Authority. 


And whereas the Competent Authority has, under sub-section () of section 6 of the said Act submitted its 
report to the Government of India. 


And whereas the Government of India after considering the said report and on being satisfied that the said 
land is required for laying the pipeline, has decided to acquire right of user therein; 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (l) of the section 6 of the said Act, the 
Government of India hereby declares that the right of user in the land specified in the Schedule appended to this 
notification is hereby acquired for laying the pipeline; 


And further, in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (4) of section 6 of the said Act, the 
Government of India hereby directs that the Right of User in the land for laying the pipeline shall, instead of vesting

in Government of India, vest, on this date of the publication of the declaration, in the Indradhanush Gas Grid Limited 
(IGGL), free from all encumbrances.

l. The Government of India, Ministry of Labour vide Order No. L-4302/l/205-IR(M) dated 25.08.205 in 


exercise of the power conferred by clause (d) of sub-section (l) and sub-section (2A) of Section 0 of the Industrial 
Disputes Act, 947 (hereinafter referred as “The Act’) (4 of 947) referred the following Industrial Dispute to this 
Tribunal for adjudication: 


300 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : APRIL 8, 2026/CHAITRA 28, 948 [PART II—SEc. 3(ii)] 
SCHEDULE 


“Whether the action of the management of M/s Hutti Gold Mines Ltd., Hutti, Raichur, Karnataka, in 
terminating the services of Sh. Ibrahim S/o Shekh Imam Sab, a temporary worker, w.e.f., 8.07.2002 is 
proper, legal and justified? If not, to what relief the said workmen are entitled to?” 


2. On receipt of the reference and on registering it as CR 28/205 and on issuance of notices to both the Parties, 
Adv. N M Handral filed vakalath for the I Party and Adv. M R C Ravi filed vakalath for the II Party. 


3. The I Party filed his claim statement stating that he was appointed as a temporary employee on 28.06.2002 
for a period of two years in Mining section; that the I Party has stated that their services would be made permanent in 
the pay scale of Rs. 800 — 050 with other benefits attached to G2 Category; that their services would be terminated if 
their services were not satisfactory; that the I Party and others were given dresses, cap etc., which were essential for 
the purpose to discharge the duty; that the Executive Director has appointed them, whereas, the Junior Officer has 
cancelled their appointment under the impugned order dated 8.07.2002; that the I Party discharged his duty without 
any complaint; that no reasons were assigned before issuance of termination order dated 8.07.2002; that he 
approached the Hon’ble High Court in WP No. 44526-44527/2002 and the Writ Petition came to be allowed; 
aggrieved by the above order the II Party has filed Writ Appeal No. 86/2003 c/w 6375/2002; that during the 
pendency of the Writ Appeal both the parties have filed Joint Memo of Settlement and the said Writ Appeal came to 
be disposed off; that the II Party has not complied with the terms and conditions of the Joint Memo till date though 
there was clear vacancy; that the II Party has recruited several other persons into service without affording any 
opportunity to the I Party and that he has been victimized by the disobedience of the Order of Writ Appeal and also 
violation of the terms of the Joint Memo of settlement by the I] Party. The I Party along with others filed WP 86362- 
8638/203 and also contempt of court case CCC no. 4043 — 4062 / 203 before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka 
seeking implementation of the terms of settlement in the Joint Memo. The Hon'ble High Court disposed the petition 
reserving liberty to the I Party to approach the jurisdictional court. The I Party sent several representations to the I 
Party requesting to provide employment based on the joint memo. Then , the I Party approached the RLC, Bellary 
seeking conciliation ; but the conciliation effort came to be ended in failure and the matter is referred to this Tribunal 
wherein the I Party filed the claim statement seeking a favorable answer in the schedule of reference and to grant 
reinstatement, consequential benefits and continuity of service. 


4. Inter alia, the II Party in its counter statement contended that the I Party along with few others was appointed 
on 26.06.2002 as a labourer on consolidated basis for a period of two years and that the II Party Management 
withdrew such appointments on 8.07.2002 as those appointments were not as per Recruitment rules and procedures 
of the II Party company; that the High Court of Karnataka in Writ Petition has also directed the II Party to take action 
against the Petitioners in the writ petitions including the I party if the Rules and Procedures are not followed in their 
appointments; that the said order was challenged by the II Party in WA 86I/2003 and the same was disposed of in 
terms of the Joint Memo filed along with memo for settlement dated 2].09.2005; that the I Party along with others 
filed WP No. 86362 — 8638/202 before the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka, Kalaburagi Bench alleging that his 
case was not considered while recruiting 50 technical posts, but the Hon’ble High Court dismissed the same on 
24.0.203 and then the I Party filed contempt petition which came to be dismissed as withdrawn; that the Order of 
appointment was withdrawn and cancelled by the competent authority and not by Junior Officer as claimed by the I 
Party; that the I Party was employed for a period of two weeks i.e., from 29.06.2002 to 8.07.2002; that as the 
appointment was discovered to be contrary to the rules of the company, the appointment orders were withdrawn vide 
order dated 8.07.2002; that the I Party cannot claim employment in the II Party as a matter of right and hence there is 
no question of any violation of the terms of settlement by the II Party; that the I Party has submitted a representation 
and an endorsement was given on |3.09.202 but informed the I Party that the Posts called for were purely technical 
posts comprising of ITI and diploma Holders and his case would be considered during the general recruitment of non- 
technical post as and when vacancies arise; that the conciliation proceedings were conducted before the Regional 
Labour Commissioner, Bellary which resulted in this reference; that the II Party has not violated any order of terms of 
settlement of the Joint Memo and that the I Party has not been victimized in any manner. Hence, the II Party has 
requested this Tribunal to dismiss the reference. 


5. After completion of the pleadings, the matter came to be posted for Evidence. On 30.0l.20l9, my learned 
Predecessor on verification of the reference Order directed to both parties that the matter may be adjudicated on 
hearing arguments and posted the matter for arguments on merits. 


6. In addition to the schedule of reference, my learned predecessor in Office on scrutiny of the rival pleadings 
put forth by the respective parties framed the following issues for consideration and disposal of the matter: 


i. Whether the II Party proves that the termination order dated /6,07.2002 is fair and proper and 
justified under the law without conducting any enquiry and without providing an opportunity to 
the I Party? 


ii. Whether the II party proves that non consideration of the representations submitted by the I 
Party as per the joint memo dated 22. //.2005 in WA 7667//2003 c/w 6375/2002 is justified? 


(ART are 3(ii)] __ भारतकाराजपत्र : अप्रैल 8, 2026/चैत्र 28, ।848 —“—i‘—isSSLTL 


ili. Whether the II Party proves that sufficient opportunity has been given to the I Party as per the 
joint memo filed by both parties in WA /667/2093 c/w 6375/2002 and also as per clause 3 of the 


settlement? 
7. Heard the detailed arguments addressed by counsel for both parties. 
8. Issues no. I to 3: Since the crucial points to be discussed and adjudicated in the given case lie inter mixed 


and intertwined, all these issues are discussed together for the sake of brevity and clarity. 


9. Undisputedly, the I Party was inducted to the pay roll of the वा Party management under Annexure A order of 
appointment dated 28.06.2002. The English translation of Annexure A which is in Kannada version reveals that the II 
Party Hutti Gold Mines Company LTD has appointed the I Party, Sh. Ibrahim, for a period of 2 years from 
28.06.2002 as an ordinary worker in the Gene division Drilling and Blasting Department (Batch no. 673) subject to 
certain terms and conditions. His salary is shown as a consolidated figure of Rs. !550/- during the first year and Rs. 
650/- during the second year per month. It is also stipulated in the order of appointment that until the administration 
confirms his appointment, he has to be continued as a temporary worker and he would be confirmed in the salary 
scales of 8000-l050, basic salary of Rs. 8000/- , FDA Rs. 35/-, VDA Rs. 745.80 and with applicable IDA. 
Surprisingly as per Annexure 8 dated 8.07.2002, the II Party management has withdrawn the appointment of the I 
Party and the same is cancelled with immediate effect and he was asked to contact the accounts department for 
settling his account. Annexure A order of appointment cautioned the I Party workman that if prior to the period of 
confirmation, his efficiency in the work and conduct are found to be not good, he would be terminated from the 
service without any prior warning or any kind of enquiry and reckoning of the period of his service will come to an 
end then and there. Annexure B, as rightly urged by the learned counsel for the I Party did not contain any specific 
reason for his termination. 


0. Eventually the termination of service was challenged by the I Party and yet another co-employee before the 
Hon'ble High Court by filing WP no. 44526 & 44527 / 2002. The order in the said writ petition reveals that several 
other writ petitions were filed by the similarly placed workmen as WP no. 2996 - 29222 / 2002 and those were stood 
disposed off on |!.!0.2002 under Annexure D order. Annexure D order would indicate that the stand adopted by the 
II Party management was that the Executive Director of the company, just before his retirement, by playing fraud has 
issued appointment to all the petitioners and on coming to know about the same, the company has withdrawn the 
appointments as the said appointments were found to be a fraud played by the Executive Director concerned and the 
writ petitioners. Under Annexure D order dated |.0.2002, the Hon'ble High Court quashed the termination order 
(Annexure B) reserving the liberty to the II Party to take action against the petitioners if really they have been 
appointed contrary to the provisions of the Recruitment Rules holding that the order of termination is bad in law since 
no opportunity is given to the writ petitioners before terminating them. The above verdict in the writ petition was 
challenged by the II Party management before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Bangalore in WA no. 
86/2003 (SRAG). During the pendency of the writ appeal , an agreement was entered into between the I Party 
workmen and the II Party management arriving at certain terms of settlement. Accordingly, the Hon'ble High Court 
disposed the writ appeals in terms of the Joint Memo filed along with the memo of settlement dated 2.09.2005. Now 
the grievance of the I Party is that despite making repeated representations requesting to provide an employment in 
the II Party company in terms of the Joint Memo of Settlement (Annexure E) aforementioned, the II Party did not 
oblige to the same. 


Il. The I Party has placed on record Annexure G representations to the Chairman of the II Party company, 
Annexure H is the representation dated I.0!.20l2 to its Executive Director and Annexure M and N respectively 
dated 7.0.20l4 and 6.2.20l4 seeking employment. Apparently no action is ensued in favor of the I Party 
pursuant to any of such request letters. Annexure O dated 08.04.20I5 is seen to be the request made by the I Party 
before the Regional Labour Commissioner, Bellary seeking for conciliation in matter narrating the whole episode. 
Annexure P is the conciliation failure report submitted by the RLC, Bellary to the Secretary, Government of India, 
Ministry of Labour and Employment dated 06.05.20I5. In Annexure O and P, the fact that the I Party has acquired the 
qualification of ITI in Electrical is made mention of. In pursuance of failure of the conciliation efforts, he rushed to 
this Tribunal seeking redressal of his grievance alleging refusal of compliance of the terms of settlement by the 
employer. 


2. All along the II Party has expressed its stand that the I Party cannot claim employment in the II Party 
company as a matter of right and hence there is no question of any violation of terms by the II Party. The II Party has 
preferred to emphatically specify certain terms of the settlement (Annexure F) viz. at clause 3 which speaks about 
cancelation of the entire selection list and disentitlement of the other persons (emphasis supplied) who were in the 
original list to be considered or given preference for any employment as per the terms of settlement. As per the said 
clause, their case will be considered depending on the merits as and when notification for recruitment is published and 
they should not claim employment as a matter of right. Now the management is very much upon this particular clause 
no. 3 to decline the urge for employment raised by the I Party. It is worthy in the context to reproduce the terms of 
settlement entered into between the parties in the Joint Memo:- 


30I2 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : APRIL 8, 2026/CHAITRA 28, 948 [PART II—SEc. 3(ii)] 


4... It is agreed that the respondent Nos. / & 2 in WA No. /667/2003 and respondent Nos. I to 27 in WA No. 
6375/2002 who were in the original selection list of //7 employees shall be considered for employment and 
they shall be given preference as and when any vacancy arises and when the management decides to fill up 
the above post. 


2. The respondent Nos. / & 2 in WA No. /66//2003 and respondent Nos. / to 27 in WA No. 6375/2002, if and 
when they are appointed, they shall be appointed as fresh employees and they shall not be entitled to any 
back wages or continuity of service or any other compensation whatsoever from the date of termination i.e., 
46.07.2002 #॥ the date of their fresh employment. 


3. Since the entire selection list has been cancelled, no other person who was in the original list shall be 
considered or given preference for any employment as per this terms of settlement. However, their case will 
be considered depending on the merits as and when notification for recruitment is published and they 
should not claim employment as a matter of right. 


4. It is agreed that even in respect of respondent Nos. I & 2 in WA No. /667/2003 and respondent Nos. / to 27 
in WA No. 6375/2002 preference shall be given in the appointment provided they fulfill all the eligibility 
criteria including medical fitness and subject to the reservation policy. However, only eligibility regarding 
age shall be relaxed. 


5. Both the parties agreed to file this joint memo before this Hon'ble High Court and pray for disposal of the 
above Writ Appeals in terms of this settlement between the parties, in the interest of justice and equity. 


3. As per clause no. | quoted above, the II Party management has agreed to give preference to the I Party and 
similarly placed 28 other persons in the original selection list, which stood cancelled, as and when any vacancy arises 
and when the management decides to fill up the above posts. Giving preference in which area is not very beautifully 
worded in clause no. | to the terms of settlement. By signing the Joint Memo, the I Party as one among the signatories 
agreed to the terms (in clause no. 2) that if and when appointed, he shall be appointed as a fresh employee and shall 
not be entitled for any back wages or continuity of service or any other compensation whatsoever from the date of 
termination i.e. 8.07.2002 till the date of his fresh employment. 


4. Clause 3 to the terms of settlement has already been discussed in the aforesaid paragraph. By the very terms 
of clause 3 referred to above, it stood appear that the said clause does not pertain to the writ petitioners in the 
respective writ petitions, numbering 29 in total. Instead the term “no other person who was in the original list” should 
be with reference to the rest among the total !7 employees in the original selection list and who did not pursue any 
litigation pursuant to the termination. As against that, the management is relentlessly using afore-quoted clause no. 3 
as a tool to discard the request of the I Party for getting an employment in the company. Failure to offer employment 
to the I Party does not tantamount to violation of terms of settlement according to the II Party simply by virtue of the 
impact of clause no. 3. However a strict interpretation of clause no. 3 as indicated by me above saves the I Party from 
its adverse application as it strictly applies to other persons (emphasis supplied) in the original list. Therefore, refusal 
to induct the I Party by offering a job, which he has applied for abundantly immediately pursuant to the disposal of 
WP 86/2003 and continuously thenceforth as and when vacancies were notified is not a fair and genuine approach 
of the II Party. 


5. Controversy exists regarding the status of the I Party at the very induction to service under the II Party. 
While the I Party claimed that he was appointed to a technical post under Annexure A appointment order dated 
28.06.2002, the II party Management opposed the said contention and urged that he was appointed only as an 
ordinary worker in G-division in the Drilling and Blasting department. A perusal of the English translation of 
Annexure A would show that appointment of the I Party under Annexure A was as an ordinary worker and not to a 
technical post. Annexure B termination order also does not bring out any divergent meaning and substance regarding 
the status of the employee in the temporary appointment. The I Party has no case that at the time of his appointment 
under Annexure A dated 28.06.2002, he had any technical qualification to be appointed at the technical post requiring 
specialized skill / experience. So apparently there cannot be any successful debate by the I Party on the status of his 
job under Annexure A order of appointment. 


6. However it is well come out in records that during the post-termination interregnum, the I Party has passed 2 
years ITI course in Electrical in the year 20l2 by securing 572 out of 700 marks (8.7] %). This is an additional 
academic qualification he claimed to have obtained at a later point of time, precisely in 20l2. On such academic 
acquisition, the I Party is seen to have applied for the post: G-8 grade vacancies with the pay scale of 20920-42660 + 
IDA applicable. The aforementioned application is accompanied with by the employment notification released by the 
II Party dated 5.03.2024 for Grade 5 posts and Grade 8 posts. The particular branches of Grade 8 posts shown in the 
employment notification are ITI fitter Mine division - 54 vacancies, ITI Fitter Metallurgy Division — |7 vacancies, ITI 
fitter Land Acquisition Mine Division — 02 vacancies; ITI (Electrical Technical Department) — 4 vacancies and 
Security guards — 24 vacancies. 


7. While the I Party has produced only the front page of the vacancy notification dated 5.03.2024 which lacks 
complete details of the prescriptions mandated by the establishment, the latter has produced the complete notifications 


[भागता--खण्ड 383)| __ भारतकाराजपत्र : अप्रैल 8, 2026/चैत्र 28, ।848 Ci 


along with its memo dated 06.03.2025 that actually shows how many vacancies arose under each head and which all 
vacancies are meant for such an such categories and all. 


8. Before entering into a detailed discussion of aforementioned vacancy notification dated 5.03.2024 produced 
by the II Party, I find it very pertinent to note that though in the memo dated 03.0.2025 the I Party has stated that he 
has put in an application for the post of Security Guard announced in the job notification dated 5.03.2024 and copy 
of the same is produced along with the memo, what is seen enclosed with the memo is an application sent by him on 
6.04.2024 to the post of ITI (Electrical) (Engineering department). The application for the post of Security Guard 
claimed to have been submitted by him is not produced before this Tribunal by the I Party. However, in the 
endorsement made by the II Party dated 26.04.2024 (in Kannada language the translation of which is produced by the 
I Party) it is made clear that the I Party has submitted an application to the Administrative Department on 28.03.2024 
which should be to the post of Security Guard announced under the aforementioned notification dated 5.03.2024. In 
the aforementioned endorsement dated 26.04.2024, the II Party management made it clear that the I Party has to 
submit PUC qualification documents to the Company. Similar statement is made by the II party in the memo dated 
7.02.2025 as well undertaking that the company would consider the application placed by the I Party to the Security 
Guard post if he has completed PUC and he filed his application with requisite educational documents if he had 
completed his PUC as on 2002-2003 whereon the II Party will verify with regard to the age relaxation and take further 
steps. The very same memo speaks about an endorsement of the II Party dated 3.09.20l2 (Annexure J). The said 
endorsement is stated to be in response to the I Party’s representation dated 25.08.20l2 as referred to in it. As 
mentioned in Annexure J, the aforementioned representation of the I Party is requesting to consider him for 
appointment in the then recruitment notification of |50 posts. Those 50 posts as declared in the aforementioned 
Annexure J endorsement were that of technical posts comprising of ITI and diploma holders and there is a solemn 
declaration by the II Party that the management is still bound to the terms of settlement made before the Hon'ble High 
Court in WA 86/2003 and that the request of the I Party would be considered during the General recruitment of 
non-technical post as and when the vacancies are called for. 


9. So much so, the application admittedly submitted by the I Party for Security Guard post (Non-technical) 
under employment notification dated 5.03.2024 is liable to be preferentially considered by the II Party management 
in strict and scrupulous compliance to the terms of the Joint Memo recorded by the Hon'ble High Court in WA 
86/2003, according the eligible / permissible age relaxation provided he submits the requisite educational 
qualification (PUC). 


20. It is the case of the I Party that in the year 20l2 he has acquired an additional academic qualification in ITI 
Electrical in a 2-year course by securing 8!.7!% of marks. This subsequent academic acquisition did enable him to 
apply for technical post of Fitter as well under the employment notification dated 5.03.2024. He has submitted copy 
of the job application dated 6.04.2024 submitted to the post of G-8 grade vacancies on a pay scale of Rs. 20920 — 
42660 + IDA applicable under category 2(b) under Preference Local as per the aforesaid notifications dated 
5.03.2024. Among the 2 notifications dated 5.03.2024, the one prescribed for Kalayana Karnataka Local cadre is 
applicable to the I Party. The said notification provides that the number of posts — ITI Fitter Group II (Mines 
Division) reserved for women is liable to be filled by men candidates after securing exemptions from the competent 
authority since underground mining work is difficult to be performed by women candidates. The I Party being a 
member of 2(b) category as claimed by him, his maximum age limit under the notification for the post of ITI Fitter 
Group II (Mines Division) is 38 years. As per the Article 37] J of the constitution of India, a special scheme is 
provided for Kalayana Karnataka job reservations which includes further age relaxation as well typically extending 
upto l0 years beyond the standard age limit envisaged by the State Government of Karnataka to support candidates 
from the designated Kalyana Karnataka districts, which also the management is bound to take into consideration 
while dealing with his job application. 


2I. An emphatic argument is set forth by the learned counsel for the II Party that the I Party is not entitled to 
apply for the technical post, as in the Joint Memo, the management has committed to give priority / preference to the 
job which he already performed under the management under Annexure Al. To put it differently, it is the case of the 
respondent that under the strength of the Joint Memo , the I Party cannot claim any preference or priority for technical 
job under the II Party management. On a close scrutiny of the specific terms and stipulations in the settlements / Joint 
memo, no such reservation / specification is seen emphasized regarding the category of job for which the I Party is 
entitled for preference / priority when such vacancy arises. It is more specifically and precisely mentioned in clause 2 
to the terms of settlement that the I Party, if and when appointed , shall be appointed as fresh employee and shall not 
be entitled to any back wages or continuity of services or any other compensation whatsoever from the date of 
termination i.e., 8.07.2002 till the date of their fresh employment. Further in clause 4, it is stipulated that preference 
shall be given in the appointment provided the I party fulfills all the eligibility criteria including medical fitness and 
subject to reservation policy ; however only eligibility regarding age shall be relaxed. There also it is not specified 
that he or any of the signatories to the Joint memo / terms of settlement shall apply only to the original post to which 
they were absorbed under Annexure Al. The fact being so , the II Party management should not add or subtract any 
condition which the joint memo / terms of settlement never intended. It is of crucial significance that this joint memo 
containing the specific terms of settlement has already been duly recorded by the Hon'ble High Court and the verdict 
in WA 86] / 2003 and the connected writ appeal is given in accordance with that. Therefore the II Party management 


304 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : APRIL 8, 2026/CHAITRA 28, 948 [PART II—SEc. 3(ii)] 


is not permitted to introduce its own interpretations to the terms and stipulations to the settlement arrived at by the 
parties. Accordingly the II Party is bound to reckon the application submitted by the I Party on 6.2.2024 to the 
technical post of ITI fitter in Group II (Mines division) under the notification dated 5.03.2024 subject to his 
eligibility for age relaxation under Article 37l-J of the Constitution of India afore-discussed by me in para 20 as on 
the date of his application. The stand adopted by the II Party that he is not at all eligible or entitled for a technical 
post sounds untenable and unsustainable and hence the said argument is discarded. It is contextually significant to 
observe that the I Party workman was not kicked out from the job for any of his proved fault / misdeed. Practically, he 
has been running from pillar to post all along till date and his grievance still remains unattended. Being a signatory to 
the consciously accepted terms of settlement, the II Party management is legally and morally duty bound to commit 
itself to the exact terms by providing eligible employment to the signatory employees under it. 


ads To conclude, the II Party is obliged to consider both the applications submitted by the I Party for the post of 
Security Guard and ITI Fitter in Group II (Mines division) as the case may be, with requisite relaxation in age as per 
the rules and Government notifications discussed supra subject to the educational qualifications required for the posts, 
giving preference to the application submitted by him to the technical post Fitter (Electrical) and to consider the same 
in a just and fair manner protecting the interest of the I Party. 


23. The I Party in his claim petition has put forth the claim for reinstatement, back consequential benefits and 
continuity of service. Indeed Annexure F terms of settlement very specifically stipulates in clause 2 that he is not 
entitled to any back wages or continuity of services or any other compensation whatsoever from the date of 
termination i.e., 8.07.2002 till the date of his fresh employment. Therefore being a signatory to Annexure F Joint 
Memo, the I Party is not entitled to claim any such extra benefits which are not permitted under the terms of 
settlement. Therefore the above relief put forth by him is untenable and unsustainable and hence is liable to be 
rejected. 

24. The schedule of reference made by the Central Government and Issue no. | framed by my Learned 
Predecessor are regarding propriety, legality and justification of the action of the II Party management in terminating 
the services of the I Party w.e.f I8.07.2002. By consciously entering into Annexure F terms of settlement with the II 
Party during the pendency of WA 86I/2003 which has been recorded and got merged in Annexure E verdict 
rendered by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the said Writ Appeal dated 22..2005, apparently the I Party has 
relinquished his challenge on his termination under Annexure B. Instead his entire claim for employment has been 
transformed to purely based on the specific terms of settlement in Annexure F, which strictly rules out any future 
claim for back wages or continuity of services or any other compensation whatsoever from the date of termination 
ie., 8.07.2002 till the date of his fresh employment. So much so, the instant Central Reference is liable to be 
answered in such a way awarding the relief specifically mentioned in para 22 above, which the II Party as a signatory 
to Annexure F Joint Memo / settlement is obliged to perform. With this view, these issues are answered accordingly. 


25. All the pending interlocutory applications are also disposed off accordingly. 
26. On this finding, the following Award is passed: 
AWARD 


The reference is thus answered by directing the II Party to consider both the applications submitted by the I 
Party for the post of Security Guard and ITI Fitter in Group II (Mines division) as the case may be, with 
requisite relaxation in age as per the rules and Government notifications subject to the educational 
qualifications required for the posts, giving preference to the application submitted by him to the technical 
post Fitter (Electrical) and to consider the same in a just and fair manner protecting the interest of the I 
Party within a period of two weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this Award.

By order No.L-40/56/20l6(IR(B-D) Dated: 8.08.207, the present industrial dispute has been referred 
for adjudication in exercise of the powers conferred by clause (d) of sub-section (l) and sub-section (2A) of Section 
0 the Industrial Disputes Act, 947 (/4 of 947) by the Central Government, with following schedule: 


"Whether the action of the management of Chief Factory Manager, Loco Workshop, NR, Lucknow, in 
denying the payment of Instructor Teaching Allowance #0#77.70,2005 to Shri Akhilesh Chandra is 
justified and legal? If not, what relief Shri Akhilesh Chandra is entitled to?" 


(ART ars 3(ii)] __ भारतकाराजपत्र : अप्रैल 8, 2026/चैत्र 28, ।8488  .__.____ 30[7 
Accordingly, an I.D. Case No. 40/207 has been registered. 


I have heard learned counsel for parties, perused the record. 


On 6.04.2004, respondent/competent authority of Northern Railway, Charbagh, Lucknow, invited 
application in order to appoint on the post of Instructors in scale of Rs.4500/- to Rs.7000/- pm to work in BTC (Basic 
Training Centre) LOCO Workshop Northern Railway Charbagh, Lucknow. 


Shri Akhilesh Chandra Dwivedi/claimant who was working as Junior Progressive Man under respondent 
no. |/Chief Factory Manager, LOCO Workshop Northern Railway, Charbagh, Lucknow, applied for his candidature. 


Thereafter a written test was conducted on 24.02.2005, candidates who are found eligible for the post of 
Instructor as per advertisement dated 6.04.2004, have been called for written test. 


Claimant/workman, appeared in written test, was passed, thereafter called for interview conducted on 
7.06.2005, declared successful. 


On 7.0.2005, workman was posted as Instructor in Grade of Rs.4500-7000, post of Instructor is an Ex 
Cadre post. 


Further as per the pleading in claim statement, workman pleaded that in his parent cadre, he was also 
promoted in Grade of Rs. 4500-7000 w.e.f. 26.05.2005 much before his posting in Ex-Cadre Post of Instructor. 


It has been further pleaded in the claim petition under existing scheme the workman who services has been 
utilized against the post of instructor, he is entitled to receive the benefit of payment of 5% extra salary of his basic 
pay, and allowance drawn by him from the date of working as instructor but the opposite parties did not make the 
payment of said 5% instructor allowance to workman concerned from the date of posting from !7.l0.2005 to 
28.2.203 against the post of Instructor. 


Further it has been pleaded on behalf of workman that he performed his duties against the post of Instructor 
in Grade 4500-7000 w.e.f. 7.0.2005 to 28.02.203 but was not paid I5% allowance on his basic pay despite the fact 
he was entitled to get said allowance from opposite parties under existing Rules, so he submitted several 
representations to get the benefit of said 5% benefit and in response of the same the General Manager/Mech Baroda 
House, New Delhi held the workman entitled to receive the teaching/instructor allowance to workman but opposite 
parties deliberately with held the payment of Instructor allowance. For which the workman is actually entitled to 
receive from opposite parties for the period he rendered his duties against the post of instructor under opposite parties. 


On behalf of workman it has also been pleaded that as per the facts and circumstances as mentioned above it 
may be held that action of management of Chief Works Manager, LOCO Workshop N.R. Lucknow in denying the 
payment of Instructor/teaching allowance from 7.0.2005 to Shri Akhilesh Chand Dwivedi is neither legal nor 
justified, and the workman may be held entitled to receive |5% Instructor teaching allowance from 7.0.2005 to 
28.02.203 the period during which he performed his duties as Instructor. 


On behalf of respondent in written statement the case which was taken up that as per office order dated 
7.0.2005, respondent is not entitled for any instructor/teaching allowance (शिक्षण भत्ता) because as per order dated 
7.0.2005, by which petitioner was sent/appointed as Instructor/Teacher the said appointment was for fixed term 
only, and in the same it was specially mention that while working the post of Instructor/teacher, he is not entitled for 
any teaching allowance as such he cannot claim the benefit as prayed by him in the present case, so the same is liable 
to be dismissed. 


Thus on the basis of pleading/document filed by parties, in short the controversy to be considered in the 
present case is “Whether the applicant/Shri Akhilesh Chandra Dwivedi is entitled for Teaching Allowance/fem भत्ता, 


while he was worked as Instructor/Teacher in the System Technical School, Northern Railway Charbagh, or not? 
As per undisputed facts of the present case in response to advertisement dated 6.04.2004, the person who 
was working in LOCO Workshop Northern Railway, Charbagh, Lucknow, were invited to submit their application for 


appointment/filling up for the post of Instructor in the scale of Rs.4500/- to Rs.7000/- pm to work in BTC (Basic 
Training Centre) LOCO Workshop Northern Railway Charbagh, Lucknow. 


In response to the same, workman submitted his candidature and declared successful. 


And on 6.08.2005, an order was issued by respondent no.2/Principal, System Technical School, Northern 
Railway, Charbagh, Lucknow, reproduced herein below:-

AWARD 


The Government of India, Ministry of Labour by its order No. L-202/84/2000-IR(B.I) dated 4.07.2000 
referred the following dispute under section l0()(d) of the I.D. Act, 947 to Industrial Tribunal No.I, Hyderabad for 
adjudication and later the same has been transferred to this Tribunal bearing ID No.72/2000, as per orders of Central 
Government vide Lr.No.H-!026/I/200l-IR(C.I]) dated 8.0.200, requiring this forum to decide the question: 


SCHEDULE 


“Whether the action of the management of State Bank of India, Dharmavaram Branch in terminating 
Sri P. Sathyanarayana Messenger, from the services of the Bank by way of oral orders w.e.f. 3.03.997 is 
justified? If not, what relief he is entitled?” 


After receipt of the reference, it was numbered as ID No. 78/2002 and notices were issued to both the 
Workman and the management. 


2: Before unfolding the factual matrix of the instant industrial dispute it would be apposite to have a bird eye 
view of a chequered history of the instant industrial dispute. Earlier instant industrial dispute along with the batch 
cases was decided by this Tribunal vide common award dated 7.5.2005 and the reference was answered in favour of 
the Respondent and against the Workman. That said common award dated 7.5.2005 was challenged by the 
aggrieved Workmen in various Writ petition No.6470/204 along with batch of writ petitions before the Hon’ble 
High Court of Andhra Pradesh and Hon’ble High Court vide its’ judgement dated 23.6.204 allowed all batch of writ 
petitions and set aside the common award dated 7.5.2005 passed in ID No.222 of 200I and other batch of ID cases 
by Central Government Industrial Tribunal cum Labour Court, Hyderabad and the Respondent management of State 
Bank of India was directed to reengage the Writ Petitioners in position, which they have been occupying prior to 
their termination and further directed to consider their cases for regularization as and when the substantive vacancy 
arises. This judgement dated 23.6.20l4 of Hon’ble High Court of AP, passed in WP No.6470/20l4 and batch 
petitions was challenged by Respondent management before the Hon’ble High Court in Writ Appeal No. 268 of 
20l4. The aforesaid Writ Appeals No.l268/20l4 and other Writ Appeals were decided by Division Bench of High 
Court of Andhra Pradesh by a common judgement dated 20.3.209. Hon’ble High Court in aforesaid Writ Appeal 
was pleased to pass the order which is extracted as below:- 


“ 7. Hearing the learned senior counsel for the SBI and the learned senior counsel for the contesting unofficial 
Respondents, we see that while the learned single Judge was justified in setting aside the award af the Tribunal, 
the proper course to be adopted was to remit all the cases to the Tribunal. This we say for reasons more than 
one. Firstly, in such matters, claims have to be decided on individual basis, as different persons have different 
claims as to the length of officiation or discharge of duties and functions; quality of engagement, drawings, 
accounting of the post for each one of them, who have worked etc. All these issues will not be the same in all the 
cases. Therefore, each case ought to have been directed to be decided by the Tribunal afresh on individual 
basis. The second and most important aspect is the learned single Judge has in one go ordered re-employment 
of all the workmen. This is not a relief that could have been granted without answering the individual issues; 
each issue relating to each case could not have been decided by the writ Court within the format of its 
adjudication procedures and scope. The adjudicating body, which has to do that activity, is the Industrial 
Tribunal. Therefore, we are of the view that while we would sustain the order of the learned singe Judge insofar 
as it interfered and sets aside the award of the Tribunal, the further findings and directions, issued through the 
impugned order have to go and the individual cases have to be sent back for consideration of the Tribunal. Such 
further procedure before the Tribunal will have to be carried forward with the materials already on record and 
also by affording an opportunity to the persons, who have claims as well as the management to place their rival 
contentions and further material before the Tribunal. The learned counsel appearing for the workmen are 
Justified in pointing out that enormous delay has already happened and further action by the Tribunal in this 
line may be expedited. 


9. In the result, these writ appeals are ordered; 


3022 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : APRIL 8, 2026/CHAITRA 28, 948 [PART II—SEc. 3(ii)] 


(4) affirming the impugned common order of the learned single Judge to the extent it sets aside the common 
award dated /7.05.2005 of the Industrial Tribuna!; 


(2) the further findings and directions issued through the impugned common order are vacated: 


(3) all the matters shall be remitted to the Industrial Tribunal with a direction to dispose of them within an 
outer limit of five (5) months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order, and, 


(4) the parties to make appearance before the Tribunal on the given date.”’ 


Thus, in view of the above direction of Hon’ble High Court of Andhra Pradesh in ५४४.७.)२०.।268 of 20I4 
and batch cases. This Tribunal has taken up the matter of industrial dispute for hearing and deciding it afresh in 
view of the aforesaid guidelines laid down by the Hon’ble High Court in Writ Appeal No.l268/204 vide judgement 
dated 20.3.09. 


3. The factual matrix of instant industrial dispute as narrated by the Workman in his claim statement are that, 
the Workman joined in the service of the management institution as Messenger from 985 to 996, and has rendered 
unblemished service spreading over a period of about |2 years. The Respondent has terminated services of 
Workman by oral orders with effect from |.4.!997. Further, it is submitted that the management of Respondent 
bank decided to give a chance to temporarily employed personnel “found suitable for permanent appointment” by 
wait- listing them by offering permanent appointment or waitlisting till such opportunity arises. 


4. That on 7.!.987 a settlement was reached between All India State Bank of India Staff Federation and the 
Management of State Bank of India - settlement one, under this settlement three categories of employees were 
listed. That is, A) those who have completed 240 days in !2 months or less after .7.!975. 8) those who have 
completed 270 days in any continuous block of 36 calendar months after |.7.975. C) (i) those who have completed 
minimum of 30 days aggregate temporary service in any calendar year after .7.975 or (ii) 70 days aggregate 
temporary service in continuous block of 36 months after .7.975. 


5. The persons who satisfied in all the above 4 categories were to be interviewed by a selection committee and 
the said selection committee would determine the suitability of the said candidate for permanent appointment. 
Therefore, the bank prescribed certain qualifications and from among the candidates satisfying the qualifications the 
suitable candidates were enlisted by a selection committee. The Clause 7 of the said agreement provided with the 
selected candidate would be wait listed in order of their respective categorization and the selected panel would be 
valid upto December, 99l. Clause l0 of the settlement specifically provided that henceforth. “there will be no 
temporary appointments in the subordinate cadre”, except on a restrictive basis in the specified category, “from 
amongst empanelled candidates as per existing guidelines of the bank”. The Workman further submits that 
consequent upon the said agreement and the draft, a notification was issued in the newspapers. The last date for 
responding to the advertisement was 30.8.988. A written examination followed by viva-voce in May, 989 was 
held. A selected panel was prepared, as per Clause 7 of the agreement, ie. Settlement No.l, the selected panel was to 
be valid upto December, 99l, the Workman submits that circular was issued on 26.4.9! by the said letter it is 
mentioned that the terms of the agreement dated 7..87 was modified vide second agreement dated 6.7.88 was 
entered into between the parties. In terms of the said agreement a chance was to be given, “to all eligible temporary 
employees for permanent appointments. The appointments were against the vacancies likely to arise during the 
years 995-96, circular made it clear that in view of the enormity of the problem an extension of the currency of the 
panel, eligible temporary employees who have been empanelled could not appear in the earlier interviews and have 
been pursuing their cases thereafter, “will be given another chance to appear for interview”. 


6. Workman submits that there were total five settlements. The settlement dated 7..87 is the # 
settlement (Ex Ml), settlement dated 6.7.88 is 275 settlement (Ex M2), settlement dated 27.0.88 is the 374 
settlement (Ex M3), then settlement dated 9..9l is 47 settlement and settlement dated 30.7.96 is 5" settlement 
(Ex M6). In between there is minutes of conciliation proceedings dated 9.6.95 marked as Ex MS. That due to all 
these settlements which were extended by subsequent settlements thereby created reasonable expectations in the 
list of the selected candidates arose with that it’s a question of time their appointments or services would be 
regularized in the services of the bank. The Workman was working with the bank on temporary basis was under 
the bonafide hope that sooner his services will be regularized with the bank. He is thereby closed all his options 
elsewhere. It is needless to point out that employing person to whom hope of employment in substantial terms was 
made is a facet of Article 2| of the Constitution of India. 


Bs Further Workman submits that the Government of India issued Circular No. F-3/3/l04/87-IR, dated 
6.8.990. Under said circular the chief Executives of all public sector banks including the Management herein were 
specifically instructed that until the problem of existing temporary employees is fully resolved, no bank is permitted 
to make any permanent appointments. That some of the persons similarly situated like this Workman aggrieved by 
the inaction on the part of the management of the bank is not regularizing their services from out of the selected panel 
and not clearly focusing the vacancy position, filed W.P. No. 494/97 before Hon’ble High court of A.P.. It is 
specifically averred in the said writ petition that the Management of the bank had failed to implement the settlement 
and that it violates the various fundamental rights guaranteed under the constitution of India. The Hon’ble High

court of A.P .. by order dated 5.3.97 directed the bank to implement the settlement as amended from time to time. It 
also directed the bank to carry out the terms of settlement before the expiry of March, !997. The Hon’ble High 
Court also recorded finding that the Bank cannot escape its liability of enforcement of the Settlement. In view of the 
directions given by the High Court all candidates whose names appeared in the select panels prepared on the basis of 
the agreement entered into on !7..87 under which the panel was valid upto December, 99, and on the basis of a

upto December, 999. The other agreement dated l6.7.!988 under which the panel was valid upto !992 and on the 
basis of the settlement dated 27.0.998 whereby the panels were made alive upto 3.3.997 were under the bonafide 
impression that their cases will be considered for regularization and were living on the basis of the said reasonable 
expectation. Unfortunately, contrary to the aforesaid directions given by the High Court and contrary to the 
settlements entered into between the parties, the bank issued proceedings dated 25.3.997, dated 27.3.997 and

are in services of the bank from .4.97. The said order was followed by the Management. Aggrieved by the said

Manager and the Assistant General Manager (Respondents 3,4 and 5 therein) on 25.3.97, 27.3.97 and 3].3.97 as

8. Further, Workman submits that in the counter affidavit filed in Writ Petition No.9206/97, the bank has 
submitted that it has about 805 branches in Andhra Pradesh alone. It has stated that due to exigencies of 
circumstances and on account of the urgent need in its banks, it employed temporary employees in subordinate cadre. 
It is pertinent to mention that it does not state the urgent or need or the nature of temporary employees that it had 
engaged. Enquiry into the same would reveal that the stand taken by the bank either on the ground of urgent need or 
of temporary employees is a fagade to perpetuate unfair labour practice. It is designed to on the one hand, keep the 
employed in the erroneous zone of hope and on the other to ensure that benefits that a model employer will extend 
under various statutes to its employees is not required to be borne out by the bank. A reading of the counter affidavit 
would show that the bank would opines that being just fair and reasonable are which obviously is reprehensible and is 
a facet of unfair labour practice. 


9. The Workman submits that the bank had referred in its counter affidavit to three settlements dated 7..87, 
6.7.88 and 27.l0.88. The bank in the guise of extending the benefits of the circular of Government dated 6.8.90 
stated in its counter affidavit that as follows: 


"Government of India, vide its letter dated 6.8.990, issued guidelines to all the public sector banks with regard to 
recruitment and absorption of temporary employees in public sector banks. The said guidelines were issued to 
implement on the lines of the approach paper on the issue provided by a committee constituted in this regard. The 
Government of India guidelines made it clear that all the public sector banks may follow the provisions laid down in 
the approach paper. 


The approach paper specified that the cases of temporary employees who had put in not less than 240 days of 
temporary service in |2 consecutive Months and who are entitled to benefit of Section 25-F may be decided by 
entering into a settlement with the representative union. In respect of temporary employees who had put in less than 
240 days of service in [2 consecutive months or less, a settlement could be avoided and however if the Management 
so desired, they could enter into a conciliation settlement with the representative union. Para 6(h), it is mentioned 
that only those temporary employees who had put in temporary service of 90 or more days after .l 982 would be 
eligible for considering under the scheme. Although the Government guidelines envisaged for a settlement in respect 
of employees who had put in temporary service of 90 or more days, the bank by way of further concession entered 
into settlements Even in respect of those who had put in less than 90 days. As such, it could be Seen that the 
settlements are more beneficial to the temporary employees concerned. The approach paper also specify at para 6(c) 
that the banks would provide one time opportunity to all the temporary employees and for that purpose temporary 
employees worked in the bank on or after |.!.982 could be considered for re-employment in terms of the scheme. 
The Respondents have gone further wherein even persons working after !975 were also considered. 


As could be seen from the above, there was a genuine effort on the part of the Respondent bank to provide 
permanent employment for as many as possible subject to availability of the vacancies. 


It is further submitted that at para 6(k) of the approach paper, it was made clear that this would be one time 
exercise in full and final settlement of all the aims and disputes for the past period in respect of temporary workmen 
covered by the settlement. This would mean that the Government of India guidelines would cover only those persons 
who were temporarily employed for the period specified therein and not otherwise. As such, it is submitted that the 
Respondents have not only followed the Government of India guidelines but in fact covered cases of the employees 
who had worked for less than 90 days. As such, question of violation does not arise and in any case those were only 
broad guidelines and not directives".

0. The Workman submits that the bank also referred a subsequent settlement dated 9..99! wherein there is a

Hon’ble High Court without considering the cases of the similarly situated candidates like the Workman herein. It is 
submitted inspite of engaging fresh candidates as is now being done by the Management they would have continued 
the similarly situated candidates like the Workman herein in the services of the bank and consider their cases for 
absorption in view of the circulars issued by Central Government as well as the directions of this Hon'ble Court in 
Writ Petition No.494/97, dated 5.3.97. In view of the circulars issued by the Central Government, the Management 
should not have relied upon the settlement dated 9..!99l. Hence, the impugned action of the Management is illegal, 
unjust, violative of fundamental rights such as Articles l4,!6 and 2] of the Constitution of India. 


ll. The Workman submits that in W.P. No.494/97 filed by the union of temporary employees where in they 
have complained about the non- implementation of the settlements arrived between the parties and sought for 
absorption. Such employees in the bank services on permanent basis before the date fixed for carrying out the terms

2. Further, it is submitted that in the clause of Settlement it is specifically mentioned that the workmen to be 
absorbed/appointed in the bank prohibiting any temporary appointments subsequent to the date of settlement even the 
authorities want to make temporary appointments that should be made only from among the empanelled can be 
appointed either for temporary vacancy or permanent vacancy except from among the empanelled candidates like the 
Workman and that should be continued till they are absorbed. The management committed unfair labour practices 
and terminated the services of the candidates with effect from .4.997 which is arbitrary, discriminatory, contrary to 
their own guidelines and violative of the constitutional provisions which are guaranteed in Chapter-III of the 
Constitution of India. 


3. The Workman submits that it is strange as to how the panels were allowed to lapse by a so-called 
Memorandum of Understanding dated 25.2.997, that the action of terminating such employees like the 
Workman by virtue of an impugned oral proceedings without implementing the settlement would be illegal and unfair 
labour practice which cannot be allowed to be perpetuated. That the discontinuance of the Workman after 3.3.97 
who had served in the bank in any capacity amounts to retrenchment. It could not have been done without any notice 
and it violates Sec.25FF of the Industrial Disputes Act, 947 and the said action is violative of principles of natural 
justice guaranteed under Chapter III of the Constitution of India. This amounts to retrenchment without one month's 
notice and taken in view of such notice. Thus, the main proceedings issued by the Respondent is without 
jurisdiction and is arbitrary, illegal and therefore liable to be quashed. That the alleged Memorandum of 
Understanding dated 27.2.97, Ex.M5 does not own any legal entity, as the said Memorandum of Understanding is 
not published anywhere to brought to the notice of the Workman whose rights are being affected. It is submitted that 
Management did not adhere to the procedure envisaged by the Central Government in its' instructions dated 6.8.90 
in the year |995. The same was not followed in the year 997 despite there being vacancies. The 
management has followed the procedure of calling candidates through Employment exchange instead of giving 
chance to the empanelled candidates like the Workman here. It is pertinent to mention here that the Respondent 
Management sent letters to the all similarly situated candidates like the Workman in the month of June, 997, 
subsequent to the passing of impugned termination orders. After knowing the facts that the candidates are litigating, 
the Management refused to engage these candidates. It is once again reiterated that the panels are meant for 
absorption but not for termination. It was the duty of the Management to engage the empanelled candidates like the 
Workman even in temporary vacancies till they are absorbed permanently in regular vacancies. Hence, the action of 
the Respondent Management terminating the services of the Workman by oral order dated 3.3.97 is unjust, illegal, 
violative of principles of natural justice and hence, the Management be directed to reinstate and absorb the Workman 
and to grant all incidental and consequential benefits.

the work force as its' members espoused the cause of temporary employees who have put in less than 240 days of

temporary service in l2 calendar months in the bank and who were ineligible for any protection under Industrial

]7. Respondent contended that, in fact, the case of the Workman can be considered under all the five settlements

absorbed in permanent service as against the constitutional rights for all eligible persons to be considered for 
employment every time a vacancy arises. That the alleged dispute including the demand for reinstatement has to be 
decided in this context. It is submitted that the period of panel list got expired on 3.3.97 and it is an integral term of 
the settlement and cannot be modified in any proceedings under the law. These temporary employees who 
unfortunately could not be accommodated for want of vacancies have no further rights to be considered for 
regularization. That the Hon'ble High Court in WP No.l2964/94, held as follows, "It is needless to state that the 
settlement arrived at between the All India State Bank of India Staff Federation which, is the majority union and the 
bank Management is binding on the Workmen also. It is not at all the case of the Workman that any of the terms of 
the settlement has been violated by the bank's Management. If the Workman had worked in the bank on part-time 
basis before 3.5.94, that itself would not vest in him a right to claim that his services should be regularized on 
permanent basis against a full time cadre post. The claim put forth by the Workman in the present petition is therefore 
misconceived and not tenable. However, it is open to the Workman to claim any right which flows from the 
settlement between the union and the bank Management. As already pointed out that it is not the grievance of the 
Workman that some right which has flown from the settlement in favour of the Workman has been denied by the bank 
Management. Therefore, I do not find any ground, let alone substantial ground, to grant the kind of relief sought for 
by the Workman. Writ Petition fails and is accordingly dismissed. No costs." 


8. Further, it is contended that if the panels were not lapsed at the end of designated period and allowed to be

deprive the chances of original claimants who would Come through proper recruitment procedure. As their rights 
have been crystallized by operation of the settlements. Hence, there is no question of any Legitimate expectation 
being violated.
